Alex: ran a quick nsys capture against the staging cluster for the batch-regression repro. baseline (v2.2) vs current runtime (v2.3.1) — ~30% slower tail latency on 99th for batch sizes 6-8.
Alex: primary suspect is kernel selection: we see fallback to a generic matmul kernel instead of the tiled/packed path for sequence_len=2048.
Alex: command I used: ```nsys profile --output nsight_run --sample=none --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --capture-range=kernel --force-overwrite --target-processes all -- python bench.py --model rwinf/model-v2 --batch 8 --seq 2048``` 
Priya: can you paste the kernel timeline? any obvious small kernels spiking? :thinking_face:
Alex: paste below (trimmed):
```
Timeline excerpt (nsys):
0.000s  kernel: packed_matmul  1.2ms
0.0013s kernel: tiled_matmul   0.9ms   <-- used in baseline
0.0022s kernel: generic_gemm   3.5ms   <-- current repro frequently
0.0057s kernel: kv_cache_lookup 0.2ms
0.0059s kernel: kv_cache_insert 0.6ms
```
Alex: the tracer shows lots of `generic_gemm` launches when kv-cache miss rate hits ~12% for the batch. baseline had miss rate ~2%.
Jordan: nvprof/old traces cared about cupti metrics — did nsys warn about CUPTI mismatches?
Alex: yes. nsys output included: `WARNING: CUPTI API version mismatch (nsys: 11.5 vs driver: 12.2) - metrics disabled` — so some kernel-level metrics (SM occupancy, achieved_occupancy) were unavailable.
Sam: okay that explains missing occupancy numbers. but why would kernel selection flip? compiler heuristic picks tiled_matmul only if workspace estimate < X and if sequence length distribution aligns. could kv-cache misses change the sequence length distribution seen by the scheduler?
Priya: also check kernel selection table (we have a runtime decision tree). maybe a recent change in batching heuristics for latency SLOs forces smaller internal micro-batches, which increases effective seq_len per kernel call.
Alex: reproduced locally in a container with nvidia-driver 535.104.05 and nsys 2024.2 — same behavior. On bare-metal with driver 510.47.03 and nsys 2023.5 baseline-like results (tiled_matmul chosen).
Jordan: drivers matter. there's a known driver Reg-4577 in release notes around 535 that changed kernel launch scheduling and preemption heuristics. could influence timing windows that the runtime uses to aggregate micro-batches.
Sam: two things to iterate: 1) repro with full CUPTI metrics enabled (so we can see SM occupancy), 2) add a short diagnostic in the runtime to log which kernel decision path was taken and the workspace estimate.
Alex: attempted CUPTI enable inside our rootless container and hit permission error from nsys: `CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PROCESS` + container attach fail. infra-bot, any CI agent notes?
infra-bot: CI job `perf/2468` ran a rootless trace yesterday; note: nsys requires access to /dev/nvidia* plus trace attach perms. Rootless builds will need `--privileged` or CAP_SYS_ADMIN and proper uidmap. See https://git.internal/infra/nvidia/rootless-notes
Priya: we shouldn't require privileged by default. can we fallback to `nvtx` annotations and perfetto with user-level sampling if CUPTI not available?
Sam: yes, but perfetto sampling has coarser granularity for kernel launch ordering. still useful. For CUPTI we can also try an older nsys that bundles a CUPTI shim compatible with driver 535.
Alex: quick diff of our runtime heuristics: we lowered the micro-batch aggregation threshold from 128ms to 64ms (PR #4821) to reduce SLO p50. That could cause fewer kernels to be batched together, increasing per-kernel overhead and kv misses.
Jordan: aha. if micro-batch size decreases, we lose prefix reuse across requests -> kv-cache miss spike. kv miss increases generic_gemm usage because quantized tiled path expects contiguous KV sizes.
Priya: propose short plan:
- collect full nsys traces on bare-metal driver 510 and 535 (to isolate driver effect) (Alex)
- enable verbose kernel-decision logging behind env flag to gather workspace and predicate (Sam)
- reproduce with perfetto user sampling to capture ordering when CUPTI unavailable (Priya)
- roll back PR #4821 in a canary to verify perf delta (Jordan)
Alex: I'll attach two traces to the ticket: link1 (bare-metal 510) and link2 (staging 535). Also exporting the timeline csv.
Alex: timeline csv snippet: ```time,kernel,name,ms
0.001,generic_gemm,3.5
0.004,tiled_matmul,0.9
0.006,kv_cache_lookup,0.2
```
Sam: if rollback proves it, we should have a short-term mitigation: when kv-cache miss rate > 8% trigger an aggressive prefetch or a 'force-tiled' hint to the kernel selector. That avoids a full rollback.
Priya: also we need to handle CUPTI mismatch gracefully in our docs and devex: detect `CUPTI API version mismatch` and print recommended nsys/driver combos and a reproducible local command.
Jordan: can someone try nsys 2023.5 with driver 535 in staging? if metrics are disabled it will still capture timeline but not occupancy. that helps isolate driver vs batching.
Alex: on it. kicking a run now (nsys job id: 67291).
infra-bot: started perf job 67291 on staging-agent-4. Logs: https://ci.redwood/perf/67291
Sam: one more note — I saw a kernel preemption trace in perfetto on 535: small kernels preempted by long-running memory copies. That could change the effective latency ordering and the runtime's latency-based batching heuristic. Add 'preemption_count' to our runtime metrics.
Priya: agreed. let's keep changes behind flags and revert quickly if needed.
Alex: thanks all — I'll post attachments and a short repro script in the ticket. If anyone can run quick local checks with older drivers, ping me. :thumbsup:
Sam: putting a follow-up todo in the perf board: PF-982 investigate tiled vs generic selection on drivers 510/535, add forced-hint experiment.
Jordan: FYI I filed an external bug with NVIDIA (case #INC-8892) referencing CUPTI API mismatch and potential scheduler change.
Alex: end of thread for now — will update when traces uploaded.
